brief: Engineering drawings of 25 mechanical parts and assemblies, 446 sheets in all, in three tiers: 8 easy sets (two of them assemblies of 8–10 parts), 7 medium and 10 hard (complex castings and assemblies of 14–26 parts). The drawings use first-angle projection in millimetres, and only all the sheets of a set read together define its part or assembly.

ul: Dimensions follow drafting practice: chain dimensions, relative positions, diameters and radii, angles and depths. They must be worked along the chain step by step, not copied as coordinates from the origin.
There are inclined faces, holes at arbitrary angles, fillets and chamfers; every feature marked R or C must be modeled.
Each part is written as a sequence of features: extrude, revolve, add, cut, hole, fillet, chamfer, pattern, mirror; assemblies also give every part's position and orientation.

Commands or scripts may display, list and sort the existing fields of the JSON dimension catalog, and the isometric preview may be run, several problems at once if wanted. Dimensions and geometry must be worked out by hand: no program may calculate, rebuild or compare shapes, and no CAD or edits to the supplied tools.

points: **Reading across views**: match the principal views, sections, auxiliary views and details to trace nested cavities and skew passages.
**Dimension chains by hand**: add up chain dimensions, find coordinates and convert the tilt and bearing of inclined holes, all by hand.
**Feature modeling**: break each shape read from the sheets into extrusions, revolutions, holes, fillets and chamfers with the right parameters and positions.
**Complex assemblies**: up to 26 parts, each placed and oriented from fits, coaxial features, mating faces and locating features.
scoring: **Tools first**: the grader reads the answering record first. Displaying, listing or sorting the catalog and previewing several problems at once are allowed; computing dimensions, deriving or rebuilding geometry with a program, using CAD or editing the tools scores the whole answer 0.

**Surfaces at two tolerances**: the model descriptions are built into solids and their surfaces compared with the reference at 0.2 mm and at 2 mm. Each tolerance gives $F = 2PR/(P+R)$, with P weighted by submitted surface area and R giving every reference face equal weight; $F^* = 0.8F_{0.2} + 0.2F_{2}$, so the loose tolerance counts for only 20%.
**Translate only**: one translation for the whole problem is found at 0.2 mm and reused at 2 mm, never a rotation; a problem earns $w \times \min(1, F^*/0.99)$.

**Assemblies and failures**: parts are matched by their parts-list number under the same translation; each tolerance pools all submitted surfaces and all reference faces, and a missing part's faces count as 0. A part whose feature fails counts as the solid before that feature; the other parts are unaffected.
**Three tiers**: problems 01–08 are worth 3.5 points each, 09–15 4 points, 16–25 4.4 points; 100 in all.
